title: Mask R-CNN
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: Instance segmentation must detect every object and precisely segment each instance, but the prevailing Faster R-CNN pipeline was not designed for pixel-to-pixel alignment: RoIPool quantizes coordinates, causing misalignment that hurts pixel-accurate masks, while per-pixel multi-class softmax couples segmentation with classification.
statements: Instance segmentation requires detecting all objects in an image while also precisely segmenting each instance.
Faster R-CNN was not designed for pixel-to-pixel alignment between network inputs and outputs, and RoIPool performs coarse spatial quantization.
Standard FCN per-pixel multi-class categorization couples segmentation and classification, which works poorly for instance segmentation.
Within-category overlapping instances are a core difficulty of instance segmentation.

evidence.quote: Instance segmentation is challenging because it requires the correct detection of all objects in an image while also precisely segmenting each instance.
Most importantly, Faster RCNN was not designed for pixel-to-pixel alignment between network inputs and outputs.
These quantizations introduce misalignments between the RoI and the extracted features.
FCNs usually perform per-pixel multi-class categorization, which couples segmentation and classification, and based on our experiments works poorly for instance segmentation.
We argue that within-category overlap is a core difficulty of instance segmentation.

background.summary: The paper builds on the Fast/Faster R-CNN detection framework, the FCN segmentation framework, FPN backbones, and prior instance-segmentation systems (DeepMask, MNC, FCIS). The claimed gap: no existing framework provides a simple, fast, enabling system for instance segmentation with proper pixel alignment.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: base detection framework extended with a parallel mask branch
relatedWork.quote: Faster R-CNN [36] advanced this stream by learning the attention mechanism with a Region Proposal Network (RPN).

relatedWork.name: Feature Pyramid Network (FPN)
relatedWork.relation: backbone architecture adopted for feature extraction
relatedWork.quote: We also explore another more effective backbone recently proposed by Lin et al. [27], called a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN).

relatedWork.name: FCIS
relatedWork.relation: prior state-of-the-art instance segmentation system with systematic errors on overlapping instances
relatedWork.quote: But FCIS exhibits systematic errors on overlapping instances and creates spurious edges

relatedWork.name: RoIPool
relatedWork.relation: prior RoI feature extractor whose quantization the paper removes
relatedWork.quote: RoIPool [12] is a standard operation for extracting a small feature map (e.g., 7×7) from each RoI.

evidence.quote: Our goal in this work is to develop a comparably enabling framework for instance segmentation.
these advances have been driven by powerful baseline systems, such as the Fast/Faster RCNN [12, 36] and Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) [30]

solution.summary: Mask R-CNN extends Faster R-CNN with a parallel fully convolutional branch that predicts a binary mask per class for each RoI, and replaces quantized RoIPool with a quantization-free RoIAlign layer so that features align pixel-to-pixel with the input.
solution.approach: Add an FCN mask branch and a RoIAlign layer to Faster R-CNN, training jointly with a multi-task loss L = Lcls + Lbox + Lmask where masks are predicted per class with a per-pixel sigmoid.
components: parallel mask branch: FCN predicting an m x m binary mask per RoI for each class
RoIAlign: quantization-free RoI feature extraction using bilinear interpolation
per-class mask prediction with per-pixel sigmoid and binary cross-entropy (decoupled from classification)
multi-task loss L = Lcls + Lbox + Lmask
backbone choices: ResNet-C4 and ResNet-FPN (also ResNeXt)

evidence.quote: The method, called Mask R-CNN, extends Faster R-CNN by adding a branch for predicting an object mask in parallel with the existing branch for bounding box recognition.
To fix the misalignment, we propose a simple, quantization-free layer, called RoIAlign, that faithfully preserves exact spatial locations.
we predict a binary mask for each class independently, without competition among classes, and rely on the network's RoI classification branch to predict the category.
removes the harsh quantization of RoIPool, properly aligning the extracted features with the input.

experiments.summary: The paper evaluates instance segmentation, bounding-box detection and person keypoint detection on COCO (trainval35k/minival/test-dev) with extensive ablations, plus an appendix on Cityscapes; it compares against MNC, FCIS/FCIS+++, Faster R-CNN variants and the COCO 2016 challenge winners.

evidence.quote: Without bells and whistles, Mask R-CNN surpasses all previous state-of-the-art single-model results on the COCO instance segmentation task [28]
RoIAlign improves AP by about 3 points over RoIPool, with much of the gain coming at high IoU
Mask R-CNN is simple to train and adds only a small overhead to Faster R-CNN, running at 5 fps.

limitations.summary: The authors note the design is not optimized for speed, that the ResNet-101-C4 variant is slow and not recommended, that adding the keypoint branch slightly reduces box/mask AP, and that Cityscapes results suffer from a persistent val/test domain shift in low-data categories.
items: Speed/accuracy trade-offs are not optimized (varying image sizes and proposal numbers is left beyond scope).
The ResNet-101-C4 variant takes about 400 ms per image and is not recommended in practice.
Joint keypoint training slightly reduces box/mask AP and does not help the other tasks.
Persistent domain shift between Cityscapes val and test for truck, bus and train categories despite COCO pre-training.

evidence.quote: Although Mask R-CNN is fast, we note that our design is not optimized for speed, and better speed/accuracy tradeoffs could be achieved [21], e.g., by varying image sizes and proposal numbers, which is beyond the scope of this paper.
However, adding the keypoint branch reduces the box/mask AP slightly, suggesting that while keypoint detection benefits from multitask training, it does not in turn help the other tasks.
This suggests that there is a domain shift on these categories, which also have little training data.

futureDirections.quote: More complex designs have the potential to improve performance but are not the focus of this work.

futureDirections.quote: better speed/accuracy tradeoffs could be achieved [21], e.g., by varying image sizes and proposal numbers, which is beyond the scope of this paper.

futureDirections.direction: Apply the framework to other instance-level recognition tasks.
futureDirections.quote: Given the effectiveness of Mask R-CNN for extracting object bounding boxes, masks, and keypoints, we expect it be an effective framework for other instance-level tasks.

equations.name: mask loss
equations.expr: Lmask = average binary cross-entropy of a per-pixel sigmoid, defined only on the ground-truth class k

deploymentClaims: Runs at 5 fps (about 200 ms per frame) on a GPU.
The shared ResNet-101-FPN model runs at 195 ms per image on an Nvidia Tesla M40 GPU.
The ResNet-101-C4 variant takes about 400 ms per image and is not recommended in practice.
Training ResNet-50-FPN on COCO trainval35k takes 32 hours on a synchronized 8-GPU machine.

evidence.quote: Our models can run at about 200ms per frame on a GPU, and training on COCO takes one to two days on a single 8-GPU machine.
This model runs at 195ms per image on an Nvidia Tesla M40 GPU
so we do not recommend using the C4 variant in practice.
